principles.name: Protect a small chip lead by trading down and refusing to overcommit after 1:00 remaining
principles.trigger: We are AHEAD by any tower-HP margin (track: our focus tower's dealt damage > damage taken on our most-damaged tower), match time <= 1:00 remaining (single-elixir or just into double), and an enemy push is forming.
principles.action: Switch to pure defense: only spend elixir on units that kill the incoming push with a positive elixir trade (e.g. Knight to tank+pull, Archers/Musketeer to DPS from behind the tower). Do NOT start a counter-push that empties your hand. Keep >= 4 elixir banked to answer the next play. Let the clock run; the chip lead is the win condition.
principles.rationale: In Arena 1-6, a fraction-of-a-tower lead wins on the time/score tiebreak if no tower falls. The failure mode is throwing away the lead by greedily attacking and getting counter-pushed. Defense + clock is the highest-EV line once ahead late.

principles.name: Press the focus tower hard during double elixir when even, ignore the other lane
principles.trigger: Match time <= 1:00 remaining (double elixir active, ~2:00 mark onward) AND tower-HP differential is roughly even (no clear lead), AND focus tower is the lower-HP of the two enemy towers.
principles.action: Build a single committed push in the focus lane: tank (Giant/Knight) at back, then add 1-2 support (Musketeer/Archers/Mini P.E.K.K.A) behind it as elixir regenerates to ~8+. Funnel everything into the already-damaged focus tower to convert the existing chip into a crown. Never split a unit to the fresh lane.
principles.rationale: Double elixir is when leads are made. Pouring fresh elixir into the tower that already has accumulated chip needs far less new damage to crown it than starting over on the full-HP tower, so the marginal elixir is most efficient there.

antipatterns: Splitting damage across both enemy towers so neither ever falls and the chip lead is too small to matter on the tiebreak.
Switching the focus tower mid-match (e.g. attacking left then right) because a unit happened to spawn there, resetting all accumulated chip progress.
Fireballing/Zapping the enemy tower for pure chip early game when no units are hit, bleeding a negative elixir trade every cycle.
Starting a fresh counter-push while already ahead in the last minute, emptying the hand and getting punished by an enemy counter that crowns OUR tower and erases the lead.
Sending the win-condition tank alone over the bridge with zero support repeatedly, feeding it to defenders for no tower damage instead of using cheap throwaway chip troops.
Holding the damage spell all game 'for value' and never using it as the literal finishing blow when the focus tower is in spell-kill range in overtime.
Ignoring an incoming enemy push to keep chipping, trading your own near-full tower for a few hundred chip damage (net tower-HP loss).
Treating overtime as 'attack everything': blindly committing both lanes in tiebreak and getting three-crowned instead of defending the lead and forcing first-tower wins.

dimension: Opening moves: best first plays (often wait/cycle a cheap card at the back), do not leak elixir, gather information

principles.name: Hard-stall at full elixir during the opening double-elixir-build phase
principles.trigger: match_time < 0:08 elapsed (i.e. first ~8 seconds), our_elixir < 10, AND enemy has played zero cards (no enemy units on the arena, enemy elixir bar visually low/unknown)
principles.action: Play NOTHING. Let elixir fill to exactly 10/10. Do not place any card while elixir < 10 and no enemy action exists to respond to. The single passable exception is starting a back-corner cheap cycle once elixir HITS 10 (see rule 2), never before.
principles.rationale: The opening of every match is a pure information game. Whoever commits first reveals their deck and cedes the initiative. Holding to 10 elixir loses nothing (you cannot bank past 10, but you also haven't leaked because the cap is not reached until ~9.5s from 0) and forces the opponent to either reveal first or also stall. At Arena 1-6 most opponents over-commit early; waiting punishes that for free.

principles.name: Avoid the elixir-cap leak: spend the cheapest card the moment you would overflow 10
principles.trigger: our_elixir == 10 (capped) AND no enemy unit is on our side of the river requiring an immediate defensive response
principles.action: Drop your cheapest cycle card (e.g. Skeletons / Goblins / Ice Spirit / Minions, 1-3 elixir) at the BACK of the arena behind the King tower or just in front of it, on whichever lane you intend to pressure. Never let the bar sit at a full 10 for more than ~1 second of regeneration time, because every second at 10 is wasted regen (a leak). Prefer the 1-2 cost card so you re-open headroom immediately and keep the cheapest pieces in rotation.
principles.rationale: Sitting at 10/10 throws away ~1 elixir every 2.8s (1x) / 1.4s (2x). That is the only real 'leak' in the opening. Spending the absolute cheapest card at the back converts wasted regen into a developing push or a cycle while committing the least information and the least counterable value. Back placement means the card walks the full lane, giving you maximum time to react to the opponent's response before it reaches their tower.

principles.name: Back-corner placement only, never bridge/front, for the opening cycle card
principles.trigger: We have decided to play a card during the opening (elixir at/near 10, no urgent defense), AND it is a non-spell, non-defensive-reaction card
principles.action: Place it in the back corner tile on your side (behind the King tower, far back-left or far back-right depending on target lane). Do NOT place at the bridge, do NOT place in the center, do NOT place in front of your own Princess tower mid-lane.
principles.rationale: Back placement gives ~6-8 seconds of travel time, during which the opponent must reveal a counter or let it through. If they reveal a counter, you have gathered information and can prepare your support; if they do nothing, you get chip + a built elixir advantage. Bridge/front placement is committal, immediately threatens, and invites a same-elixir trade that surrenders the information edge. It also lets the opponent counterpush directly into your side.

principles.name: Never open with a spell or a high-cost win condition
principles.trigger: It is the opening (first play of the match) AND the candidate card is a spell (Arrows, Fireball, Zap, etc.) OR a 4+ elixir win condition (Giant, Hog Rider, Balloon, P.E.K.K.A) AND there is no enemy target on the field
principles.action: Skip that card. Filter the opening-play candidate set to cheap cycle cards (1-3 elixir, non-spell) only. Hold spells and win conditions until you have either a confirmed target (spell) or a built elixir lead / known enemy hand (win condition).
principles.rationale: Opening a spell with no target is a guaranteed total-value leak (the elixir hits nothing). Opening a heavy win condition with no support and a full enemy hand walks it into the opponent's strongest unrevealed counter at parity, the worst possible information position. Both are classic naive-bot blunders. Cheap cards keep options open and information cost minimal.

principles.name: If the enemy commits first to one lane, respond on the SAME lane and prepare a counterpush, do not mirror-leak on the other lane
principles.trigger: Enemy places a unit/win condition at their bridge or back on a specific lane (lane = left or right) AND we have not yet committed our opening card
principles.action: Do not pre-emptively dump a card on the opposite lane. Hold elixir, let the enemy unit cross the river, and place your defensive/counter card on the SAME lane positioned to kill it (e.g. cheap swarm in front of a ground push, or air-targeting unit vs air). Then ride the surviving units back as a counterpush. Only after defending do you consider an offensive opening.
principles.rationale: Splitting your response to the opposite lane while they push yours leaks elixir on a non-threat and lets their push hit your tower at a discount. Defending on-lane and counterpushing is the highest-value opening response: you trade down, gain tempo, and learn their lead card. This is the single most important reactive opening pattern at low arenas where opponents lead with their win condition blindly.

principles.name: Track and remember the enemy's first revealed card to anticipate their cycle
principles.trigger: Enemy plays their first card (any time in opening) — record its type, elixir cost, and lane
principles.action: Store enemy_revealed_cards += this card. Do not immediately counter-commit beyond what the threat requires. Use the revealed card to bias your next placements: e.g. if they revealed a swarm (Goblins/Skeleton Army), keep a small spell or splash unit in hand; if they revealed a tank, prioritize building a defensive distraction. Withhold your own win condition until at least one enemy card is known so you can place it in the lane opposite their counter.
principles.rationale: Card tracking is the core of the information game. At Arena 1-6 opponents typically have a single answer to your win condition; knowing what they've shown lets you time your push for when that answer is out of cycle. The opening is when the cheapest information is gathered, so the bot must explicitly log it rather than react play-by-play with no memory.

principles.name: Mirror the stall: if both sides hold and elixir caps, take the cheap-cycle initiative on your stronger lane rather than waiting indefinitely
principles.trigger: match_time elapsed > 0:10, our_elixir == 10, enemy_units == 0 (enemy also stalling), no enemy card revealed yet
principles.action: Break the standoff by cycling your cheapest card to the back corner of your INTENDED push lane (the lane away from where you expect their counter, or simply your default win-condition lane). This starts building toward your win condition on a chosen lane while staying at minimal information cost. Do not over-invest; one cheap card only, then refill.
principles.rationale: Once both players are capped at 10, continued waiting becomes a mutual leak; the symmetry is broken only by spending. The cheapest possible spend on a chosen lane is the lowest-information, lowest-cost way to seize tempo and avoid throwing away regen. It also begins shaping the match toward your game plan instead of passively reacting.

principles.name: Do not pre-place anti-air or splash 'just in case' before any enemy unit exists
principles.trigger: It is the opening, no enemy unit is on the field, AND candidate action is a defensive structure or defensive troop placed reactively-without-a-target (e.g. Cannon, Tesla, Musketeer placed in the back with nothing to shoot)
principles.action: Do not place defensive buildings/troops speculatively in the opening. Hold them. Only deploy a defensive building when an enemy win condition is committed and crossing, and place it on the 4-tile-from-river center 'pull' spot to maximize lane control at that moment.
principles.rationale: Speculative defense in the opening commits your counter before you know the threat, reveals your defensive answer for free, and often gets out-of-cycle by the time the real push arrives. Buildings especially have a deploy-then-decay clock; placing early wastes their lifespan. Hold the answer until the question is asked.

antipatterns: Opening by playing a card the instant elixir reaches 4-5 (premature commitment) instead of waiting toward 10 — reveals your hand first and cedes the information edge.
Leading with the win condition (Giant/Hog/Balloon) at the bridge on the first play with no support and a full enemy hand — walks it into the opponent's strongest unrevealed counter at elixir parity.
Casting a spell (Arrows/Fireball/Zap) as the opening move with no enemy target on the field — a 100% wasted-elixir leak.
Placing the opening cycle card at the bridge or in front of your own tower instead of the back corner — gives the opponent no travel time to react to and surrenders counterpush potential.
Sitting at a capped 10/10 elixir for multiple seconds 'waiting for the perfect play' — silently leaks ~1 elixir every 1.4-2.8s of regen.
Splitting a response onto the opposite lane while the enemy pushes your lane — leaks elixir on a non-threat and lets their push chip your tower for free.
Pre-placing a defensive building or anti-air troop speculatively before any enemy unit exists — reveals your answer and wastes the building/troop lifespan clock.
Ignoring/forgetting the enemy's first revealed card and reacting move-to-move with no memory — throws away the cheapest information in the match.
Dumping two or three cards in the opening to 'apply pressure' before elixir or information justifies it — over-commits, leaks tempo, and gets counterpushed.

Mirroring the opponent's exact lane and card to 'trade evenly' in the opening — converts a free information-gathering window into a neutral parity trade that benefits the player with the better deck/skill.

dimension: Low-arena matchups (Arena 1-6): beating beatdown/Giant push, swarm spam, spell-bait, and hog/fast-cycle with a starter-style deck (Knight, Archers, Musketeer, Mini P.E.K.K.A, Giant, Spear Goblins, Goblins, Arrows, Fireball, Minions, Bomber, Skeletons style cards)

principles.name: Never open by committing high-elixir win condition first
principles.trigger: match_time < 0:20 (first 20s of single-elixir) AND no enemy unit has crossed the river AND our elixir < 7
principles.action: Do NOT play Giant or any 4+ elixir card at the bridge. Either hold (let elixir bank to 10) or place a cheap defensive/cycle card (Skeletons, Spear Goblins, 1-2 elixir) at the back near the King tower to scout enemy reaction.
principles.rationale: Opening with the win condition lets the opponent counter-push into your weakest defensive state and discover your archetype. Reacting first preserves an elixir/information advantage that decides low-arena games where players overcommit.

principles.name: Counter Giant beatdown: ignore the Giant, kill the support, swarm the tank
principles.trigger: Enemy Giant detected on enemy side (HP > 1500, moving toward a tower) AND one or more support troops (Musketeer/Archers/Wizard/Witch) placed behind it
principles.action: First, kill the support with a spell or a unit that outranges it: drop Musketeer/Archers on the OPPOSITE side of the support troop so the Giant cannot body-block, or Fireball/Arrows the clustered support if 2+ squishy units are grouped within one spell radius. Then place a high-DPS melee unit (Mini P.E.K.K.A or Knight) directly on top of the Giant once it is past the river so it tanks for nothing. Use the tower as your third damage source. Do not waste any card on the Giant alone until its support is dead.
principles.rationale: The Giant only deals tower damage; its support is what kills your defenders. Removing support first turns the Giant into free elixir. Mini P.E.K.K.A kills a Giant in roughly 4-5 hits; placing it on top minimizes the Giant's tower damage.

principles.name: Pull the tank to the center with a building/cheap unit to split the push
principles.trigger: Enemy Giant (or Giant Skeleton/Royal Giant) committed to ONE lane AND it is approaching the bridge AND we have a building or a cheap melee unit available
principles.action: Place the defensive building (Cannon/Tombstone if in deck) or a cheap melee distraction (Knight/Goblins) in the dead-center tile between the two lanes / just inside the river on your side, so the Giant retargets toward the middle and walks diagonally. This drags the Giant away from the tower and buys 2-3 extra seconds of free defensive DPS while the support gets stranded.
principles.rationale: Center placement pulls single-target tanks off the direct tower path. Every second the Giant spends rerouting is free tower/defender damage and prevents a deep penetration.

principles.name: Counter swarm spam (Skeleton Army, Goblin Gang, Minion Horde, Barbarians) with splash, not single-target
principles.trigger: Enemy plays 3+ small units (Skeletons, Goblins, Minions, Spear Goblins) simultaneously OR a horde card (Skeleton Army ~15 units, Minion Horde 6 units) on offense or to defend
principles.action: Respond with splash: Arrows (kills Skeleton Army, Goblins, Minion Horde, Princess outright), Bomber, Wizard, or Valkyrie. Use Arrows on ground horde / Minion Horde; use a Fireball only if the swarm is clustered with a support troop to two-for-one value. NEVER answer a swarm with a single-target unit (Musketeer/Mini P.E.K.K.A) alone. If swarm is defensive Skeleton Army on your tank, drop Arrows preemptively as the tank crosses.
principles.rationale: Splash damage one-shots swarms for a guaranteed positive trade; single-target troops get surrounded and die. Arrows at ~3 elixir kills a ~3-4 elixir swarm for clean value.

principles.name: Beat spell-bait: do NOT use your splash spell on the bait card
principles.trigger: Enemy repeatedly plays cheap bait targets (Goblin Barrel, Goblin Gang, Skeleton Army, Princess, Dart Goblin) trying to draw out Arrows/Log/Fireball
principles.action: Hold your area spell. Defend the cheap bait with troops where possible (Knight/Archers tank-and-kill a Goblin Barrel; let the tower + a single unit handle Goblin Gang). Save Arrows/Fireball exclusively for the high-value target the opponent is hiding (their Minion Horde, their Princess, or a stacked counterpush). Only spend the spell when it kills 2+ units or a key squishy support, never on a lone bait.
principles.rationale: Spell-bait decks win by trading their 3-elixir bait for your 3-elixir spell, then punishing the lane your spell can no longer defend. Refusing the bait collapses their whole game plan.

principles.name: Goblin Barrel specifically: pre-place a unit on the tower or tap the tower
principles.trigger: Enemy has shown Goblin Barrel before AND enemy elixir suggests a barrel is coming (or barrel animation thrown toward our tower)
principles.action: Drop a small splash/cheap unit (Knight, Archers, Bomber, or Skeletons) directly onto the tower's expected landing tile so the goblins are damaged/distracted on landing; the tower finishes them. Reserve Arrows ONLY if you cannot react in time, since the opponent wants that Arrows trade.
principles.rationale: Three goblins do heavy DPS if unanswered, but a single body on the tower plus tower hits clears them for ~2 elixir or less, denying the bait trade.

principles.name: Counter Hog Rider / fast cycle: building or surround, defend at the tower not the bridge
principles.trigger: Enemy Hog Rider (or Battle Ram/Ram Rider) crosses the bridge targeting a tower AND match_time is in single-elixir
principles.action: Place a defensive building (Cannon/Tombstone) 4 tiles in front and slightly center of the threatened tower to pull the Hog away, OR if no building, surround the Hog with a cheap swarm (Skeletons/Goblins/Spear Goblins) placed slightly behind-and-beside the Hog so it cannot one-shot them and they out-DPS it. Knight placed on top also tanks 2-3 Hog hits. Accept ~1 small jump hit max; the goal is to give up at most one connection.
principles.rationale: Hog cycle wins by chip + cheap repeated pressure. A building resets its target every cycle for a positive elixir trade (Cannon 3 < Hog 4) and forces them to over-invest to break through.

principles.name: Punish over-commitment on the opposite lane
principles.trigger: Enemy has dumped a heavy push (Giant + 2 support, or big swarm) on ONE lane AND their elixir is read as < 4 (low) AND our defense is stable / win condition (Giant/Hog) available
principles.action: After your defense neutralizes their push, immediately send your win condition + any surviving defenders down the OPPOSITE lane. Place Giant/Hog at the bridge so the counterpush hits before they regenerate elixir to defend.
principles.rationale: Low-arena opponents overcommit and can't defend two lanes. The counterpush off a successful defense is the single highest-EV play in the format because their elixir is spent and your defenders are already on the field free.

principles.name: Defend efficiently to build a counterpush, never trade negative
principles.trigger: Any incoming enemy push AND our elixir <= enemy committed elixir
principles.action: Choose the cheapest card combination that fully neutralizes the threat (e.g., Knight + Archers vs a Giant+Musketeer), placing defenders so survivors live to counterpush. Prefer units that survive (Knight, Musketeer) over chump blocks when ahead on elixir; prefer minimum-elixir trades when behind. Always keep at least one splash answer (Arrows) in hand if the enemy deck contains a swarm.
principles.rationale: Low-arena games are won on cumulative elixir advantage. Surviving defenders convert defense into offense; negative trades compound into a lost tower.

principles.name: Double/triple elixir (last 60s + overtime): switch to spell cycle and lane focus
principles.trigger: match_time >= 2:00 (double elixir) OR overtime AND towers are even or we are ahead by one tower
principles.action: Commit fully to ONE lane with win condition + full support stack since elixir regenerates fast enough to defend the other lane reactively. If a tower is low (< 400 HP), cycle Fireball/Arrows directly to the tower for the finish when no troop can reach it. If ahead, defend conservatively and only counterpush; do not open new offense that can be punished.
principles.rationale: In 2x/3x elixir, big pushes are sustainable and chip spells close games. Single-lane focus overwhelms the reactive defender; protecting a lead by trading down wins the clock.

principles.name: Track and respect the enemy's splash/spell so your swarm is safe
principles.trigger: Enemy has used Arrows/Fireball/Log/Zap recently (within ~last cycle, card on cooldown)
principles.action: When their splash answer is known-spent, deploy your swarm (Goblins/Minions/Skeletons) as offense or value defense, because they cannot instantly clear it. Conversely, if their splash is UP, do not bunch your small units; spread placements or lead with a tank.
principles.rationale: Swarm value is entirely conditional on the opponent's splash availability. Exploiting the spell-down window is free damage; ignoring it feeds clean spell value.

principles.name: Air threats (Minions/Minion Horde/Baby Dragon): answer with ranged, never melee
principles.trigger: Enemy deploys any air unit (Minions, Minion Horde, Baby Dragon, Balloon)
principles.action: Defend with ranged anti-air: Archers, Musketeer, Spear Goblins, or Arrows (Arrows one-shots Minions/Minion Horde). For a Balloon, prioritize Musketeer + distraction and tank its hit with a building if available. Never rely on ground melee (Knight/Mini P.E.K.K.A/Valkyrie) against air; they cannot hit it.
principles.rationale: Many low-arena losses come from a melee-heavy hand whiffing on air. Keeping a ranged/anti-air card in reserve is mandatory; Arrows is the cheapest hard answer to Minion Horde.

antipatterns: Opening the match by dropping the Giant (or any 4+ elixir win condition) at the bridge on the first hand, handing the opponent a free counterpush into your empty back line.
Attacking the Giant directly with single-target troops while its Musketeer/Wizard support melts your defenders untouched.
Using a single-target unit (Musketeer, Mini P.E.K.K.A, Knight alone) to defend a Skeleton Army or Minion Horde and watching it get swarmed to death.
Spending Arrows/Fireball/Log on the FIRST cheap bait card (lone Goblin Gang, lone Goblin Barrel, single Skeleton Army) instead of saving it for the hidden high-value target.
Reacting to a Goblin Barrel only with Arrows every time, giving the spell-bait deck exactly the even trade it wants.
Defending a Hog Rider at the bridge with a unit placed in front of it, letting the Hog jump the river and get a full connection on the tower anyway.
Defending with the most expensive answer available (over-defending) and falling behind on elixir even though you stopped the push.
Bunching all your small units in a tight cluster when the enemy's splash spell is known to be available, gifting a 1-for-3 spell value.
Sending melee-only units (Knight, Valkyrie, Mini P.E.K.K.A) to deal with air troops they physically cannot target, leaving the tower to take all the damage.
Counterpushing into a full-elixir opponent instead of waiting until they have over-committed and are low on elixir.
Letting elixir sit capped at 10 for many seconds while doing nothing, leaking elixir and giving up tempo.
Ignoring lane choice in double elixir by splitting forces across both lanes so neither push is strong enough to break a tower.
Chasing a fleeing/kited unit deep into the enemy's side, walking your defenders into the enemy tower and their fresh defense.
Cycling your win condition repeatedly without support so it gets cleanly defended every time, bleeding elixir for zero damage.
